Package website

Source: .github/PAGES.md

The pkgdown workflow builds the checked-out package and its documentation on Ubuntu. Pull requests targeting master build the site and upload a reviewable github-pages artifact. Pushes to master also deploy that artifact to https://gestimation.github.io/cifmodeling/ after the build succeeds.

One-time migration

  1. Confirm that the workflow’s Build pkgdown site check passes on the PR.
  2. In Settings > Pages > Build and deployment > Source, select GitHub Actions instead of Deploy from a branch. Keep the existing site URL and domain settings.
  3. Merge the workflow PR into master. Its push run builds and deploys the current site. If it was merged before changing the Pages setting, open Actions > pkgdown > Run workflow, select master, and run it again.
  4. Confirm the Deploy pkgdown site job succeeds, then check the public version number, Reference pages and both reporting articles.

The checked-in docs/ directory is the old publication snapshot. The new workflow generates its complete site in a fresh runner-temporary directory; it neither publishes the snapshot nor commits generated files. Leave docs/ in place during this migration; removing historical generated files can be a separate cleanup after successful publication. Historical article URLs are retained through redirects in _pkgdown.yml.

Routine updates

Update R documentation, vignettes/, NEWS, or _pkgdown.yml in a normal PR. Merge into master after review; no local site build or HTML commit is needed. The root site follows master (release display mode), including when the package version has not changed. Manual runs on other branches build only.

The build installs the local package and its suggested/website dependencies, runs the examples and articles, and checks that every vignette has an article page and that both gtsummary articles contain rendered tables. Only the deploy job has Pages write and OIDC permissions; PRs do not deploy. Production runs are serialized, and a failed build leaves the last successful site online.

For a failed build, inspect the pkgdown job log and fix the source in a PR. For a failed deployment, first check the Pages source above and the github-pages environment’s deployment restrictions. The workflow uses the standard GITHUB_TOKEN; no personal access token or deploy key is needed.

References: GitHub Pages custom workflows, r-lib pkgdown workflow.
